themes_detail.label: Illegal dumping surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 2.8 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 114% increase—suggesting a new or accelerating environmental enforcement problem in Hunts Point.
evidence: 6 illegal dumping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.8-week average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 2.71, high severity)
118% spike represents statistically significant deviation from baseline behavior
Concurrent with 61% DROP in unsanitary condition complaints (15 THIS WEEK vs. 38.9 avg), suggesting possible code enforcement shift or new dumping sites
reporting_angles: Where are these illegal dumps located and what are residents complaining about?
Has DSNY or Department of Environmental Protection changed enforcement patterns or staffing in the district?

themes_detail.label: Air quality emergency signals
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints skyrocketed 540% two weeks ago (4 complaints vs. 0.6-week baseline), and indoor air quality spiked 409% last week (7 complaints vs. 1.4-week baseline)—two distinct atmospheric hazard signals in the same district within days.
evidence: Air Quality complaints: 4 two weeks ago vs. 0.6-week average (z-score: 4.85, high severity)
Indoor Air Quality complaints: 7 last week vs. 1.4-week average (z-score: 3.26, high severity)
Two separate complaint categories spiking within same 2-week window suggests broader air contamination or pollution event
reporting_angles: What industrial, vehicular, or weather-related source is degrading air quality in Hunts Point?
Are residents with asthma or respiratory illness reporting health impacts? Can NYC Department of Health data correlate with complaint spike?

themes_detail.label: Rodent infestation acceleration
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped 191% last week (4 complaints vs. 1.4-week baseline)—a sharp uptick in pest pressure that correlates with the concurrent illegal dumping spike and may indicate food/waste availability issues.
evidence: 4 rodent complaints last week vs. 1.4-week average (z-score: 2.65, high severity)
191% spike in rodent complaints coincides with 114% spike in illegal dumping complaints THIS WEEK
Suggests causal relationship: increased dumping sites create food sources attracting rodents
reporting_angles: Are illegal dump sites attracting rodents? Interview residents and DSNY about integrated dumping-and-pest problem.
What is the Health Department's rodent mitigation strategy in Hunts Point—are inspections or baiting programs keeping pace with complaint surge?

themes_detail.label: Building/use violation spike
themes_detail.summary: Building/use complaints surged 243% last week (3 complaints vs. 0.9-week baseline), coinciding with 216 DOB permit filings over 90 days (167 alterations)—suggesting potential code compliance or occupancy issues tied to ongoing construction activity.
evidence: 3 building/use complaints last week vs. 0.9-week average (z-score: 3.54, high severity)
243% spike in building/use complaints aligns with 216 DOB permit filings over 90 days, mostly alterations (167)
Community board has requested 'assign additional building inspectors' repeatedly—may signal chronic underinspection during high-activity period
reporting_angles: Are building inspectors keeping pace with 167 active alterations? Interview DOB about staffing levels in CD 202.
What specific building/use violations triggered last week's complaints—illegal occupancy, safety code breaches, unpermitted work?

themes_detail.label: Park safety and enforcement gaps
themes_detail.summary: Violation of Park Rules complaints jumped 243% two weeks ago (3 complaints vs. 0.9-week baseline), and the community board has repeatedly requested 'enhance park safety through more security staff'—indicating a sustained enforcement gap now manifesting in fresh complaints.
evidence: 3 park rules violation complaints two weeks ago vs. 0.9-week average (z-score: 2.72, high severity)
Community board has filed 'enhance park safety through more security staff' budget request repeatedly across multiple years—unmet request
Spike in complaints suggests chronic understaffing now producing visible enforcement failures
reporting_angles: Which parks in Hunts Point are generating complaints? Interview Parks enforcement about staffing and why the community board's repeated request has not been funded.
What specific park rule violations are residents reporting—loitering, unauthorized vendors, sanitation, safety hazards?
